quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and slow down to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic flow, and merge when clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic flow, and merge when clear.
questions.explanation: Do not stop. Use the acceleration lane to speed up and merge smoothly with the fast traffic on the interstate.

questions.question: A U-turn is not permitted:

options.text: In a parking lot.
On or near any curve or hill.
On a straight roadway with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near any curve or hill.
questions.explanation: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill. You cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians. This can cause a crash.

questions.question: If you are driving near a large commercial vehicle, you should:

options.text: Follow the large vehicle closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.
Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.
questions.explanation: Large commercial vehicles have large blind spots on each side. Do not drive beside them for long periods of time.

questions.question: If you approach a red traffic light and a police officer tells you to go through the intersection, you should:

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Go through the intersection without stopping.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection without stopping.
questions.explanation: Police officer instructions always override traffic signals and signs. Follow the officer's directions.

questions.question: You should always travel:

options.text: At the speed of vehicles surrounding you.
At the speed limit.
At a speed that fits the road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a speed that fits the road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Your speed should depend on road conditions, weather, and the legal speed limit. Never drive above the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: As your speed increases, the chance of death in a crash increases.
As your speed increases, you should increase your following distance.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash. At speeds over 80 mph, survival is nearly impossible. Higher speeds also require longer stopping distances, so you must increase your following distance.

questions.question: In a work zone, you should:

options.text: Watch for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers.
Slow down and obey the posted speed limit.
Follow directions from flaggers and signs.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In a work zone, watch for cones, barrels, signs, large construction vehicles, and workers. Slow down and obey the posted speed limit. Follow directions from flaggers and signs.

questions.question: Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as:

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: At speeds up to 35 mph, tires move water away from the tire. Above 35 mph, tires cannot move water as well. Your tires may lose contact with the road and slide like water skis.

questions.question: Slowing down to look at accidents or unusual sights:

options.text: Causes traffic congestion.
Prevents rear-end collisions.
Improves traffic flow by preventing collisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Causes traffic congestion.
questions.explanation: Avoid looking at accidents or unusual sights. This causes traffic jams.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance when:

options.text: Following a station wagon.
Following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.
Following a small passenger car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, or vehicles towing trailers may not see you behind them. Stay farther back. Large vehicles also block your view of the road ahead.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, what should you do?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: Slow down without braking hard. Then carefully turn back onto the pavement. Watch for other traffic as you move back onto the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No turning.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction where this sign is posted.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Pull to the right and stop.
Stop where you are immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear a siren, pull to the right side of the road and stop right away.

questions.question: What is distracted driving?

options.text: Anything that causes you to make a quick movement while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving means anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off the road. It is the most common cause of traffic crashes. Distractions cause drivers to miss important signs and sounds needed to avoid accidents.

questions.question: To be ready for anything ahead on the road, what should you do?

options.text: Look at the entire road and all sides.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Keep your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Focus only on the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and all sides.
questions.explanation: Good driving depends on finding and identifying problems before you reach them. Look far ahead, but also scan the sides of the road and the entire area around your vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: One outside mirror eliminates blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see all blind spots in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Even with rearview and outside mirrors, all vehicles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than most cars.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should check your mirrors and:

options.text: Never look over your right shoulder.
Always slow down in your lane.
Look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check behind you by looking over your shoulder. Make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Also check that no other drivers are moving into the same space from another lane.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Turn right after making a complete stop.
Right turns are not allowed.
Left turns are allowed.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right turns are not allowed.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign that shows a law you must obey. Where this sign is posted, right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Leave the car and walk for help.
Lie down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car so rescuers can find you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car so rescuers can find you.
questions.explanation: Stay in your car and wait for help. Rescuers are more likely to find you if you stay in your vehicle. Walking around in a snowstorm is dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Divided highway ends.
One-way traffic ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.
Keep to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you to stay to the right of the divider ahead.

questions.question: What should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: High beam headlights
Parking lights
Low beam headlights

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: Road hazard warning
Interstate route
School crossing
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Road hazard warning
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs are yellow warning signs. They warn you about hazards ahead or areas where special rules apply. Orange diamond signs are used in work zones.

questions.question: What is a driving distraction?

options.text: Anything that causes you to swerve while driving
Anything that takes your attention away from driving
Anything that makes you focus more on driving

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving
questions.explanation: A driving distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can happen anytime and anywhere. They can cause crashes that damage property, injure people, or cause death.

questions.question: What greatly increases stopping distance and crash severity?

options.text: High speeds
Slow speeds
Driving at night
Driving uphill

questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds
questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity. The faster you drive, the greater the impact force if you crash.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire blows out while driving?

options.text: Slam on your brakes
Hold the steering wheel tightly and slow down gradually
Keep driving normally
Turn on hazard lights and keep driving

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tightly and slow down gradually
questions.explanation: Do not brake hard during a blowout. Grip the steering wheel firmly to stay in your lane. Ease off the gas and slow down. When moving very slowly, apply brakes lightly and pull to a safe area off the road.

questions.question: When passing, when is it safe to return to your lane?

options.text: When the other driver signals you to move back
When you look back and see the car behind you
When you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror
questions.explanation: There must be a safe gap between your car and the passed car before you return to your lane. When you see both headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough space.

questions.question: Is night driving more or less dangerous than day driving?

options.text: Less dangerous
Equally dangerous
More dangerous
Easier on your eyes

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous than day driving. You cannot see as well in the dark. Headlight glare from other cars can temporarily blind you. More tired or impaired drivers may be on the road at night.

questions.question: Which statement about large trucks is true?

options.text: Trucks have larger blind spots than regular cars
You should avoid driving beside a large truck for long periods
Both of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above
questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots that extend behind the cab and along the truck's length. The driver cannot see you there. Avoid staying beside or behind large trucks for long periods.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space around your vehicle?

options.text: To prevent distractions from other cars
To give you time to react to sudden situations
To keep traffic moving at a safe speed
To keep other drivers alert

questions.correctAnswerText: To give you time to react to sudden situations
questions.explanation: Space around your vehicle gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. This is the only way to ensure you have enough reaction time.

questions.question: What is the term for the amount of alcohol in your blood?

options.text: Implied consent (IC)
Blood alcohol concentration (BAC)
Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC)

questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC)
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. A higher BAC number means you are more impaired.
